questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere out of europe, and thought that Korea would be an exciting place, with an interesting culture. I also read that the universities were good and that other students had a good experience being in Seoul.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Had a great experience, though corona restrictions made it harder to enjoy the city fully.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university was pretty helpful and answered quickly to any questions I had. I did however do a fair bit of research by myself, but it was not very dificult to find the information I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Got assistance from university on questions before arrival, but did not need much help after arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Got housing through a housing community called Simple Spaces. They were easy to find, and quickly got housing after I contacted them.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of options for off-campus living, but if you don't know anyone in the city I would recommend living in a housing community like Simple Spaces as you quickly get a network of friends in the city. I do however think there are cheaper options available.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Had to log in at night when registration opened, using a point system to choose courses I wanted. Got told that we had to use Internet Explorer to enter the website which was difficult, because I had a Mac, but it worked in the end with Google Chrome.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange student helpdesk, answers e-mails quickly and were helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: At first I only got half the courses I wanted, but after staying on the waitlist I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have a few courses you want, in case you dont get the ones you want the most. Also, the website is very slow when the application opens, but you just have to be patient and wait.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Interesting courses and good professors.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was pretty much the same in terms of academic level and workload.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more formal and less room for class discussion. Had a couple of exams that was more based on memorizing class material, but other than that it was quite similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Analysis of international financial markets
Economics of energy and science
Regional economics
International money and finance

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would recommend the course in analysis of international financial markets and economics of energy and science. They both had great professors, and exciting course material.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are a bit expensive, especially fruits and vegetables, but it is very cheap to eat out, so I did that a lot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I joined a buddy club, and went out with them one night. Very nice way of meeting people, and there were more activities with the buddy club available. 
Because of the corona restrictions there were not a lot of social activities available, that I could find. However, I had a friend who joined the Yonsei football team and seemed to enjoy that.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining a buddy club at the university.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going to Busan and Jeju, both very nice places with lots of stuff to do. In the weekends I would recommend going hiking in Seoul, there many good hikes around the city and is a great way of exploring Korea and getting out of the busy city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not very hard to adjust to the local culture, even though some things took some time to get used to. Seoul is also a very modern city, so Koreans are used to western culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I had online class, but the local students did not seem interested in socializing during class hours. I would recommend joining some social activities on campus.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Could be challenging engaging socially with Koreans sometimes, because of the language barrier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very beautiful country, with interesting culture and good food. Also loved Seoul, with endless possibilities to explore and a fun nightlife.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to have some money so you can explore other places in Korea. 
Pack some warm clothes, it gets pretty cold there in the winter. 
Sign up for the buddy program, to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Figure out the conversion from Korean credits to ECTS with UCPH. A couple of other students I met from UCPH got a different conversion than I did, and had to take more courses than I did for the same amount of ECTS.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of new people from around the world, see a lot of beautiful places and experience a new culture,

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Corona restrictions limited the possibility to meet new people, but there still ways to go out and have fun anyways.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
